description: Plays one MPX part as control voltage, the way a guitarist would: each string a channel of a polyphonic cable, its pitch carrying the bends, slides and vibrato, its gate, level and timbre shaped by how each note is played. The number of strings, their tuning and the capo come from the instrument on the cable.

params.name: Humanise
params.text: How much the timing, loudness and lengths of the notes are varied, from 0%, where the same notes come out the same way every time, through 100%, the amount the rules file sets, to 200%.

inputs.name: MPX note
inputs.text: One part: its notes and how each is played, from Guitar Chart or any MPX source.

outputs.name: Gate
outputs.text: 10V while each string sounds, one channel per string. A hammer-on or legato slide keeps the gate high rather than starting a new one.

outputs.name: 1V/oct, as played
outputs.text: Each string's pitch as played, 1V per octave with 0V at middle C, one channel per string, with the bends, slides and vibrato in it.

outputs.name: Level
outputs.text: Each string's loudness, 0 to 10V, one channel per string: the note's dynamic with its accents, ghost notes and palm mutes in it.

outputs.name: Timbre
outputs.text: Each string's brightness, 0 to 10V, one channel per string: low for a palm mute or a dead note, high for a harmonic, 6V for an ordinary note.

outputs.name: Pressure
outputs.text: Each string's pressure, 0 to 10V, one channel per string, passed through from the part when its source sends one.

outputs.name: Pan
outputs.text: Each string's place in the stereo field, -5V at the left to 5V at the right, one channel per string.

notes: A hammer-on, pull-off or legato slide sends no new gate: the pitch moves while the gate is held, so an envelope patched to the gate carries on through the change of note.
The performance rules are read from DreamerMPX/perform.txt, which is written with the defaults the first time, and read again from the right-click menu.
